problem.name: Mermin–Peres magic-square game
problem.statement_latex: A referee independently samples row $r\in\{1,2,3\}$ for Alice and column $c\in\{1,2,3\}$ for Bob. Alice outputs three signs of product $+1$ and Bob three of product $-1$; their intersection values must agree. No communication follows the inputs. Complexity uses winning probability and shared entanglement.
problem.statement_text: A referee independently samples row $r\in\{1,2,3\}$ for Alice and column $c\in\{1,2,3\}$ for Bob. strength.description_latex: A nonlocal success-probability separation at zero communication.

evidence.description_latex: The exact classical and quantum winning probabilities are proved.

hardware.description_latex: Two EPR pairs suffice; photonic experiments use polarization and orbital-angular-momentum entanglement.
hardware.description_text: Two EPR pairs suffice; photonic experiments use polarization and orbital-angular-momentum entanglement.

quantum.headline_latex: Success $1$ with two EPR pairs and constant-size local measurements. Commuting Mermin--Peres observables supply the required parities and agreement.
quantum.headline_text: Success $1$ with two EPR pairs and constant-size local measurements. Commuting Mermin–Peres observables supply the required parities and agreement.

classical.headline_latex: Optimal classical success is exactly $8/9$, allowing shared randomness and arbitrary local computation. A deterministic assignment satisfying eight of nine input pairs attains it.
classical.headline_text: Optimal classical success is exactly $8/9$, allowing shared randomness and arbitrary local computation. A deterministic assignment satisfying eight of nine input pairs attains it.
